title: Database Connection Management
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of database connection management and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the database connection management example and predict its expected result.

content.intro: Learn database connection management through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Database Connection Management matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines database connection management as part of database configuration, migrations, and transactions. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Connection lifecycle; Connection settings; Database timeouts; Connection pooling concepts; Monitoring connection utilization. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Connection lifecycle
items.text: For Connection lifecycle, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Connection settings
items.text: Configuration for Connection settings should be explicit, environment-aware, and validated before serving requests. Record defaults and deploy-specific values, keep secrets outside committed content, and test the setting that changes behavior.

items.title: Database timeouts
items.text: Database timeouts affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Connection pooling concepts
items.text: Connection pooling concepts should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Connection lifecycle. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
